questions.question_text: What is the probability of getting a sum equal to 11 when we roll 3 dice simultaneously?
questions.solution_text:
To determine the probability of getting a sum equal to 11 when rolling three dice simultaneously, we need to calculate the total number of favourable outcomes and divide it by the total number of possible outcomes.
First, find the total number of possible outcomes when rolling three dice. Each die has six faces, so there are 6 possible outcomes for each die. Since we are rolling three dice, the total number of possible outcomes is 6*6*6 = 216.
The sum of numbers should be 11
Case : When the sum is 11 (27 possibilities)
(1,4,6) - 6 possibility
(1,5,5) - 3 possibility
(2,3,6) - 6 possibility
(2,4,5) - 6 possibility
(3,3,5) - 3 possibility
(3,4,4) - 3 possibility
=> Probability = 27/216 = 9/72 = 1/8

questions.question_text: The shopkeeper bought a 60-litre oil can for Rs. 250 per litre. He divided the oil into three parts in the ratio 1:2:3 and poured them into three different cans A, B and C (all of volume 30 litres each) respectively. To completely fill the cans, he added a substandard oil priced at Rs.100 per litre. Later, he marked all three cans at Rs.10000 and while selling gave discounts of 10%, 20% and 10% respectively for Cans A, B and C. Find the ratio of profit percentage of Can A and Can C.
questions.solution_text:
The volume distribution of 60 litres of oil in three cans in a ratio of 1:2:3 will be 10 litres, 20 litres and 30 litres, respectively.
In the given question, the oil is divided into three equal cans. The first can is completely filled with 10 litres of oil at a cost of Rs. 250 per litre. Therefore, the first can cost 10 x 250 + 20 x 100 = Rs. 4500.
For the second can, 20 litres are filled with oil priced at Rs. 250 per litre and the remaining 10 litres are filled with substandard oil priced at Rs. 100 per litre. So, the cost of filling the second can is (20 x 250) + (10 x 100) = Rs. 5000 + Rs. 1000 = Rs. 6000.
Similarly, for the third can, 30 litres are filled with oil priced at Rs. 250 per litre
Thus, the cost of filling the third can is (30 x 250) = Rs. 7500.
All cans are marked at Rs. 10000 for selling.
To calculate the profit percentage, we need to determine the selling price. The selling price are as follows
Can A- 10% discount on Rs.10,000  = Rs. 9000
Can B - 20% discount on Rs. 10,000 = Rs. 8000
Can C - 10% discount on Rs. 10,000 = Rs. 9000
Profit percentage of Can A , B and C are
=> Can A = (9000-4500)/4500 = 1 = 100%
=> Can B = (8000-6000)/6000 = 1/3 = 33%
=> Can C = (9000-7500)/7500 = 1/5 = 20%
Therefore,ratio of profit percentages of A and C = 100:20
=> 5:1

questions.question_text: Captain America and Batman run a 10 km race on a circular track of length 1000m. They complete one round in 200 seconds and 400 seconds respectively. After how much time from the start will the faster person meet the slower person for the last time?
questions.solution_text:
Let us say Captain America meets Batman after t seconds he starts from the starting point. Speeds of Captain America and batman are 5m/s and 2.5 m/s respectively.
t = $\frac{1000}{5-2.5}$ = 400 seconds
Distance travelled by Captain America when meets Batman for the first time = 2000m i.e., after 2 complete revolutions. So by the time he completes 10 revolutions, he will meet Batman 5 times.
So time for $5^{th}$ meet = 400 * 5 = 2000 seconds.

questions.question_text: Shubham purchased a 2-BHK flat in Kondapur from Samay for an undisclosed amount. He spent 25 Lakhs on interior designs and furniture. Later, he sold the flat to Aditya at a 40% profit. Aditya was keen on an IoT-powered home and invested 15 Lakhs in updating the technology and installing an IoT system in the flat. He then sold the flat at 80 Lakhs higher than the price at which Samay sold it to Shubham. If Aditya earned a profit of Rs. 10 Lakhs, find the price at which Shubham sold the flat.
questions.solution_text:
Let Samay sold the flat to Shubham at Rs.$x$
The cost price for Shubham will be Rs. $x$+ 25,00,000
Hence, Shubham sold the flat for = 1.40($x$+25,00,000) = 1.40$x$+35,00,000
=> Now, Aditya further spend Rs.15,00,000 on updating the technology and installing an IoT system in the flat.
Hence cost price for Aditya = Rs. 1.4$x$+50,00,000
In the question, it is given that
=> $x$+80,00,000 - (1.4$x$+50,00,000) = Rs. 10,00,000
=> -$.4x$ + 30,00,000 = 10,00,000
=> $.4x$ = 20,00,000
=> $x$ = Rs. 50,00,000
We are required to find the  price at which Shubham sold the flat 
=> 1.40$x$+35,00,000
=> 1.40(50,00,000)+ 35,00,000
=> Rs. 1.05 Crore

questions.question_text: Sourabh invested $x$ rupees in Bank A at $8\frac{1}{3}\%$ simple interest. After four years, he withdrew all the amount and invested Rs. $2000$ in Bank B at a $41.42\%$ interest rate compounded annually and the rest of the amount in Bank C at $8\frac{1}{3}\%$ simple interest.  If, after four years of investment, the amounts of Bank C and B were equal, How much amount did Sourabh invest in Bank A? (Take $\sqrt{2}-1=0.4142$)
questions.solution_text:
Sourabh invested Rs. x in bank A at 8.33% simple interest. 
Interest after 4 years = $\ \dfrac{\ x\times\ 8.33\times\ 4}{100}=>\ \dfrac{\ x\ \times\ 4}{12}=\dfrac{x}{3}$. 
Hence, the total amount is $\dfrac{x}{3}+x=\dfrac{4x}{3}$.
Rs 2000 was withdrawn from Bank A and invested in Bank B at a 41.42% rate of interest compounded annually. He invested $\left(\frac{4x}{3}-2000\right)$ rupees in Bank C at 8.33% simple interest.
Hence, the principal amount in Bank C is Rs. $\left(\dfrac{4x}{3}-2000\right)$, and in Bank B is Rs. 2000.
After 4 years of investing in Bank C, the total amount in Bank A = P + I = $\left(\dfrac{4x}{3}-2000\right)\ +\ \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{4x}{3}-2000\right)\times\ \dfrac{100}{12}\times\ 4}{100}=\left(\dfrac{4x}{3}-2000\right)+\left(\dfrac{\ 4x}{3}-2000\right)\times\ \dfrac{1}{3}\ =\left(\dfrac{4x}{3}-2000\right)\times\ \dfrac{4}{3}=\ \dfrac{\ 16x-24000}{9}$
The total amount in Bank B = $2000\left(1+\ \dfrac{\ 41.42}{100}\right)^4\ =2000\left(1+\ \dfrac{\ 100\left(\sqrt{\ 2}-1\right)}{100}\right)^{^4}=2000.\left(\sqrt{\ 2}\right)^4=2000\times\ 4=8000$
It is given, 
$\ \dfrac{\ 16x-24000}{9}=8000\ =>16x\ =\ 96000\ =>\ x=6000$.
The answer is option D.

questions.question_text: What is the area of the unshaded region outside the regular octagon inscribed inside a circle of radius 4 cm?
questions.solution_text:
f we join the longest diagonals in the octagon, we will find 8 sectors of equal area, each subtending $\ \frac{360^{\circ\ }}{8}\ =45^{\circ\ }$ in the centre.
Area of unshaded region in one such sector= (Area of the sector- area of the triangle)= $\frac{45^{\circ}}{360^{\circ\ }}\pi r^2-\frac{1}{2}r^2Sin45^{\circ\ }$= $\ \frac{\pi r^2}{8}-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}r^2=\ 2\pi-4\sqrt{2}=2\left(\pi\ -2\sqrt{2}\right)\ $
Therefore, area of unshaded region in the entire circle= $8\times\ 2\left(\pi\ -2\sqrt{2}\right)=16\left(\pi-2\sqrt{2\ }\right)\ $

questions.question_text: The average number of patients a doctor treated on the first 6 days of a week is 25, while the average for the last 6 days is 26. If the total number of patients on the first and last day is 40, find the number of patients on the last day.
questions.solution_text:
Average patients per day = Sum of the number of patients on given days/ Total number of days
Total number of patients on first 6 day = Sum of patients from day 1 to 6= 25 X 6=150  (Total number of days=6)
Sum of patients from day 2 to 7= 26 X 6=156
Sum of the number of patients on day 1 to 6 = [1] + [2] +  [3] + [4] +  [5] + [6] = 150...(i) where [x] is the number of patients on day x
Sum of the number of patients on day 1 to 6 = [2] +  [3] + [4] +  [5] + [6] + [7]= 156 ....(ii)
Subtracting (i) from (ii)=> [7]-[1]=6, 
Also, [7]+[1]=40
Solving the two euations we get, [7]=23 and [1]=17

questions.question_text: A group of men and women can complete a work in 100 days. If two men in the group are replaced by two women, the new group can complete the same work in 80 days.  If three men in the original group are replaced by three women, then in how many days can the new group complete the same work?
questions.solution_text:
Let, a man and a woman can complete the work alone in M, and W days, respectively, and initially, the group has 'a' men and 'b' women.
Therefore, the equation will be: $\frac{a}{M}+\frac{b}{W}=\frac{1}{100}$  .......Eq(1)
When two men are replaced by two women, the number of men in the new group $\left(a-2\right)$, and the number of women in the new group is $\left(b+2\right)$.
The equation will be: $\frac{a-2}{M}+\frac{b+2}{W}=\frac{1}{80}$  ......Eq(2)
If three men are replaced by three women from the original group, the number of men in the new group is $\left(a-3\right)$, and the number of women in the new group is $\left(b+3\right)$. 
Let the work will be completed in t days. Then the equation will be: $\frac{a-3}{M}+\frac{b+3}{W}=\frac{1}{t}$ ......Eq(3)
Now, from Eq(2) - Eq(1), we get: $-\frac{2}{M}+\frac{2}{W}=\frac{1}{80}-\frac{1}{100}=\frac{1}{400}\ =>-\frac{1}{M}+\frac{1}{W}=\frac{1}{800}$ .....Eq(4)
Now, from Eq(3)-Eq(2), we get: $-\frac{1}{M}+\frac{1}{W}=\frac{1}{t}-\frac{1}{80}$  ......Eq(5)
Equating Eq(4) and Eq(5), we get:
$\frac{1}{800}=\frac{1}{t}-\frac{1}{80}\ =>\frac{1}{t}=\frac{1}{800}+\frac{1}{80}\ =\ \frac{\ 1+10}{800}=\frac{11}{800}$.
Therefore, $t\ =\ \frac{800}{11}$ days.
The correct option is C.

questions.question_text: We have a circle given by the equation $x^2+y^2-2x-2y-2=0$ and a straight line given by the equation x + y = 0 cuts the circle into two parts. Find the area of smaller part.
questions.solution_text:
Given equation of circle is $x^2+y^2-2x-2y-2=0$, It can be written as $\left(x-1\right)^2+\left(y-1\right)^2=2^2$.
This is an equation of a circle whose centre is (1,1) and has a radius of 2 units.
To find the points of intersection, we should solve the circle and line equation
=> putting $y=-x\ $ in the circle equation we get
$\left(x-1\right)^2+\left(-x-1\right)^2=4$
=> $2x^2=2$ => $x\ =\ \pm\ 1$.
Therefore, points of intersection are C(-1,1) and D(1,-1).
We see that C (-1,1) O (1,1) D (1,-1) is a right-angled triangle. To find the area of the smaller part of the circle, we can subtract the area of the triangle (OCD) from the quarter-circle.
Therefore, the area of the smaller part of the circle = $\dfrac{1}{4}\pi\ \left(2\right)^2-\dfrac{1}{2}\times\ 2\times\ 2\ =\ \pi\ -2\ $ sq. units.

questions.question_text: k is a natural number less than 1000, such that the quadratic equation $2x^2-kx+9=0$ has real roots and k has an odd number of factors. How many possible values can k assume?
questions.solution_text:
Given that 'k' has an odd number of factors.
We know that the number of factors of a number k is (a+1)(b+1)....., where a,b.. are the powers in the prime-factorisation of the k => For the number of factors to be odd, each of (a+1), (b+1) should be odd => a,b,.. should be even => k should be a perfect square.
Since the quadratic has real roots, the discriminant is greater than or equal to 0.
=> $k^2-4\left(2\right)\left(9\right)$
=> $k^2>72$
=> smallest k (perfect square) that satisfies this is k = 9.
Therefore, the possible values of k are $3^2,4^2,5^2,....31^2$ => Number of possible values of k is 31 - 3 + 1 = 29.

questions.question_text:
The values of x that satisfy the following equation are $x_1,x_2$. Find the value of $x_1^2+x_2^2$ 

$\left|x^2+4x+3\right|+2x+5\ =0$
questions.solution_text:
$\left|x^2+4x+3\right|+2x+5\ =0$
Case - 1 When $x^2+4x+3\ \ge\ 0$
=> $\left(x+3\right)\left(x+1\right)\ \ge\ 0$
=> $x\in\ \left(-\infty\ ,-3\right]U\ \left[-1,\infty\ \right)$ --------(1)
Then the equation becomes $x^2+6x+8\ =0$
=> $\left(x+2\right)\left(x+4\right)\ =\ 0$
=> $x\ =\ -2,\ -4$
=> $x\ =-2$ does not satisfy condition (1)
Therefore, x = -4 is the solution 
Case - 2 When $x^2+4x+3\ \le\ 0$
=> $\left(x+3\right)\left(x+1\right)\ \le\ 0$
=> $x\in\left(-3,-1\right)$     -----------------(2)
Then the equation becomes $-\left(x^2+4x+3\right)+2x+5\ =0$
=> $-x^2-2x+2\ =0$
=> $x^2+2x-2\ =0$
=> $x=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{\left(2\right)^2-4\left(1\right)\left(-2\right)\ }\ }{2\left(1\right)}$
=> $x=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{12\ }\ }{2}$
=> $x=-1\pm\sqrt{3}\ $
=> $x=-1\ +\ \sqrt{3}\ $ does not satisfy condition (2)
Therefore, $x=-1\ -\sqrt{3}\ $ is the solution
$x_1=-4\ $ and $x_2=-1-\sqrt{3\ }\ $
$x_1^2+x_2^2=\left(-4\right)^2+\left(-1-\sqrt{3\ }\right)^2$
=> $20+2\sqrt{3}$

questions.question_text: Saavn wanted to buy fruits worth Rs. 1000. He decided to buy some apples and bananas, which cost Rs 32 each and Rs 8 each, respectively, such that he would be left with Rs 40/-. Had he decided to reverse the number of apples and bananas he planned to buy, he would have had to spend Rs. 2880. While at the shop, he decided to buy only Chikoos, which cost Rs 12 each instead. If the total number of fruits he intended to buy remains the same, how much money would he have had to spend?
questions.solution_text:
Let the number of apples he planned to buy be "x" and the number of "y" be the number of bananas he planned to buy.
Therefore 32x+8y=960....(i)
Now had he reversed the number of apples and bananas he planned to  buy he would have exceeded his budget buy 188% which means that he would have had to spend 1880 more.
Therefore 8x+32y=2880....(ii)
Adding (i) and (ii) we get 40x+40y= 3840
Therefore x+y= 96.
As he went home with as many number of fruits as he intended to, number of Chikoos he bought =96
So amount he spent on Chikoos= 96*12= 1152 rupees.
The correct option is C

questions.question_text: If a, b and c are lengths of sides of a triangle and it is given that $c^2+\dfrac{ab}{2-\sqrt{\ 3}}=\left(a+b\right)^2$, what is the angle opposite to the side of length c?
questions.solution_text:
Given equation,
$c^2+\dfrac{ab}{2-\sqrt{\ 3}}=\left(a+b\right)^2$
Rationalising the 2nd term on the L.H.S, we get
$c^2+\dfrac{ab}{2-\sqrt{\ 3}}\times\ \dfrac{\left(2+\sqrt{\ 3}\right)}{2+\sqrt{\ 3}}=\left(a+b\right)^2$
$c^2+ab\left(2+\sqrt{\ 3}\right)=a^2+b^2+2ab$
$c^2=a^2+b^2-\sqrt{\ 3}ab$
Comparing this with co-sine rule
$c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab\cos C$
=> Cos C = $\dfrac{\sqrt{\ 3}}{2}$
=> Angle C = 30 degrees.

questions.question_text: Find the value of $x$, if $x+\log_6\left(1+2^x\right)=x\log_63+\log_612$
questions.solution_text:
=> $x+\log_6\left(1+2^x\right)=x\log_63+\log_612$
=> $\log_6\left(1+2^x\right)=x\log_63+\log_612-x\log_66$
=> $\log_6\left(1+2^x\right)=\log_63^x+\log_612-\log_66^x$
=> $\log_6\left(1+2^x\right)=\log_63^x\ \left(\frac{12\ }{6^x}\right)$
=> $\log_6\left(1+2^x\right)=\log_6\left(\frac{12\ }{2^x}\right)$
=> $\left(1+2^x\right)=\left(\frac{12\ }{2^x}\right)$
Let $2^{x\ }=t$
=> $t\left(1+t\right)=12$
=> $t^2+t-12$ = 0
=> t = -4 or +3
=> $2^x=3$
=> 1 < x < 2

questions.question_text: If the graph of $f\left(x\right)\ =\ px^3+bx^2+cx+d$ cuts the $x$ axis at -3 and 3 and the $y$ axis at 5 , the value of $b$ is?
questions.solution_text:
When the graph intersects at x axis at -3 and 3 , (-3,0) ,(3,0) are the points on the graph and similarly so is (0,5)
Now $f\left(x\right)\ =\ px^3+bx^2+cx+d$ 
$\ \ \therefore y=px^3+bx^2+cx+d$
$\ \ \therefore0=p\left(-3\right)^3+b\left(-3\right)^2+c\left(-3\right)+d$
$\ \ \therefore0=-27p+9b-3c+d$ .....(i)
Now $0$ $=$ $\ \ p\left(3\right)^3+b\left(3\right)^2+c\left(3\right)+d$
$\ \ \therefore0=27p+9b+3c+d$.....(ii)
On adding (i) and (ii) we get $18b+2d=0$....(iii)
Now considering that the graph also passes through (0,5)
5=0+0+0+d
$\therefore\ d=5$....(iv)
Putting (iv) in (iii) we get
$18b=-10$
$\therefore\ b=\ \frac{\ -10}{18}=\ \frac{\ -5}{9}$
So , Option A is correct

questions.question_text: If a car travels at 50 km/hr, it reaches its destination at 5 PM. If it travels at 60 km/hour, it reaches its destination at 4 PM. What is the speed(in km/hr) required to reach the destination at 3 PM?
questions.solution_text:
Assuming the time taken is t if travels with 50 km/hr.
Hence, distance = 50t
Also, with 60 km/hr, distance = 60(t-1)
Both distances will be equal.
Hence, 50t =60t-60
=> t=6 hrs,
So the distance = 50*6 =300km
Hence, required speed = $\ \frac{\ 300}{6-2}$ = 75 km/h

It can be shown as
One of the diagonal has a length of 10. It is possible when PR =10
only. As, PS = 6 and SR = 8
Thus we observe that PSR and PQR is a right-triangle as $6^2+8^2=\ 10^2$
Area of the land = $2\times\ \frac{1}{2}\left(6\right)\left(8\right)\ =48\ $ sq units.
Area of land 
= $\left(\frac{\ 1\ }{2}\times PR\times\ SO\right)\ +\left(\frac{\ 1\ }{2}\times PR\times\ QO\right)=48$
=> $\left(\frac{\ 1\ }{2}\times PR\times\ QS\right)=48$
$QS=\ \frac{96}{10}=9.6$ units
Therefore, the other diagonal's length (x) = 9.6 meter.

questions.question_text: A Machine Alpha can pack one thousand gifts in 8 hours, a Machine Beta can pack the same number of gifts in 10 hours, and Machine Delta can pack 480 gifts in 12 hours. All the machines start at 10:14 A.M. while machine Alpha is closed at 11:26 A.M. The remaining two machines complete work. When will the work (to pack one thousand gifts) be finished approximately?
questions.solution_text:
Let the efficiency of Alpha be "P" number of gifts per hour 
Total gifts packed by alpha in 8 hrs = 1000 nos
Gifts packed by alpha in 1 hr = 125 nos.
Similarly, the efficiency of beta is "Q" number of gifts per hour
Total gifts packed by Beta in 10 hr = 1000 nos
Gifts packed by beta in 1 hr = 100 nos.
Similarly, the efficiency of delta is "R" number of gifts per hour 
Total gifts packed by delta in 12 hr = 1000*(0.48) = 480 nos
Gifts packed by delta in 1 hr = 40 nos.
Gifts packed from 10:14 A.M to 11: 26 A.M ( Total time is 1 hr 12 minutes)
=> Gifts packed by alpha, beta and delta in 1 hr 12 minutes = (125+25+100+20+40+8) = 318 nos.
The remaining gifts were packed by beta and delta = 1000-318 = 682 nos.
=> Time taken by beta and delta = 682/140 (140 is total gifts packed by beta and delta in one hour
=> 4 hrs 52 min (approx)
Therefore, the work (to pack one thousand gifts) be finished by 11:26 + 4hrs 52 min
=> 4:18 pm

questions.question_text:
Find the product of all positive integral values of x that satisfy inequalities A and B.

A) $\dfrac{x^2-1\ }{x^2-7x+12}\ge\ 1$ 

B) $\dfrac{3x^2-7x+8\ }{x^2+1}\le\ 2$
questions.solution_text:
Solving for
A) $\dfrac{x^2-1\ }{x^2-7x+12}\ge\ 1$
=> $\dfrac{x^2-1\ }{x^2-7x+12}-1\ge0$
=> $\dfrac{x^2-1\ -\left(x^2-7x+12\right)}{x^2-7x+12}\ge0$
=> $\dfrac{7x-13}{\left(x-4\right)\left(x-3\right)}\ge0$
=> $x\ \in\ \left[\frac{13\ }{7},\ 3\right)\ U\ \left(4,\ \infty\right)$
For B) $\dfrac{3x^2-7x+8\ }{x^2+1}\le\ 2$
=> $\dfrac{3x^2-7x+8\ }{x^2+1}-2\ \le\ 0$
=> $\dfrac{3x^2-7x+8-2\left(x^2+1\right)\ }{x^2+1}\le\ 0$
=> $\dfrac{x^2-7x+6\ }{x^2+1}\le\ 0$
